lines.en: Clara, you look so happy! What was the best day of your life?
lines.pt: Clara, você parece tão feliz! Qual foi o melhor dia da sua vida?

lines.en: Easy. Last summer, we went to the beach near here.
lines.pt: Fácil. No verão passado, fomos à praia aqui perto.

lines.en: What was the weather like? Was it hot?
lines.pt: Como estava o tempo? Fazia calor?

lines.en: Perfect! The sun was shining, and the water was warm.
lines.pt: Perfeito! O sol brilhava e a água estava morna.

lines.en: What did you do there? Did you swim?
lines.pt: O que vocês fizeram lá? Você nadou?

lines.en: Yes. While the kids were building a sandcastle, I was swimming.
lines.pt: Sim. Enquanto as crianças construíam um castelo de areia, eu nadava.

lines.en: Sounds lovely. Did anything special happen?
Yes! I was sitting on the sand when my husband gave me a ring.
lines.pt: Sim! Eu estava sentada na areia quando meu marido me deu um anel.

lines.en: Wow! Were you surprised? What did you say?
lines.pt: Uau! Você ficou surpresa? O que você disse?

lines.en: I was crying, and I said yes! Everyone was clapping.
lines.pt: Eu chorava, e disse sim! Todo mundo aplaudia.

lines.en: Great news, Clara! That really was a perfect day.
lines.pt: Que notícia ótima, Clara! Esse foi mesmo um dia perfeito.

facts.label: Passado simples + past progressive
facts.sub: Conte uma história curta: past progressive para o cenário e para a ação em andamento; passado simples para os fatos principais.

facts.label: O cenário
facts.sub: Use was/were + verbo-ing para descrever o cenário: The sun was shining, and the water was warm. Isso mostra como estava o dia quando a história começou.

facts.label: Os fatos
facts.sub: Use o passado simples para os fatos principais: We went to the beach. He gave me a ring. Cada fato empurra a história para frente.

compare.ask: The sun was shining when we arrived.
compare.br: No Brasil, usamos o imperfeito para o cenário e o pretérito para os fatos: “o sol brilhava quando chegamos”.
compare.tip: Diga: “The sun was shining when we arrived.”
compare.us: Em inglês: was/were + -ing para o cenário e o passado simples para os fatos.

solo: Peça uma experiência pessoal do aluno com essa diferença.

pages.title: Mito ou fato? · 1/2

items.s: The past progressive describes the scene of a story.
The simple past is used for the main events.

pages.instruction: Decida e explique com suas palavras.

solo: Aluno responde e justifica; você mostra a pista.
group: Cada aluno decide sozinho, depois compare as respostas e peça uma justificativa.
Corrija pela pista do texto, não só dizendo “certo/errado”.
extra90: Peça que cada aluno invente uma pergunta igual para o colega.
answers: The past progressive describes the scene of a story. → Verdadeiro (Yes.)
The simple past is used for the main events. → Verdadeiro (Yes.)
We say “The sun was shine”. → Falso (We say was shining.)

pages.title: A day by the lake · 1/3
paragraphs: It is a sunny afternoon on a beach near Chicago. Small waves roll onto the shore. Clara sits on a towel with a big smile. She has sunscreen on her nose and a ring on her hand. Her friend Gina sits next to her. Gina asks about her happiest day.
“Clara, you look so happy! What was the best day of your life?” says Gina. “Easy. Last summer, we went to the beach near here.” says Clara. “What was the weather like? Was it hot?” says Gina.
